correctness.rationale: For each abstract state (b,k), three exhaustive pair-selection transitions with exact probabilities change the singleton count by 0, 1 or 2 and the cherry count by one precisely for a two-singleton merger. Independent Exp(k(k-1)/2) holding times give a b*T_k external-length increment. First-moment formulas f=b(b-1)/(3(k-1)), g=2b/k and the law-of-total-covariance recurrence yield a rational closed K(b,k). Explicit base k=3 with b<=2, separate exception k=b=3, and the all-k induction prove K(n,n)=-2/9 for n>=4 and zero for n=2,3. Finite exact comparisons (2201 states) and 56700 enumerated labeled histories at n=7 corroborate but are not used as infinite proof. Rate convention, sign and boundaries audited.

value.rationale: Cherries quantify local sister-pair topology while external length quantifies terminal genealogical time: both are standard, biologically interpretable, non-arbitrary observables. Their covariance is an unexpected exact sample-size-independent negative constant for every n>=4, despite opposing marginal-variance scales; a universal partial-state covariance kernel and a sharp n=3 boundary explain the phenomenon. The derived logarithmically vanishing correlation supplies additional structural insight rather than a tiny numerical improvement. The result is not a recomputation of the marginal cherry or external-length distributions.
